transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Hi, thank you. Well, what brought me in is that... I keep getting up in situations where everyone else is seated. 

It happens a lot in staff meetings at my school, or even just sitting at the dinner table. I'll suddenly feel this need to get up—like, I'll go refill my coffee, or go check a handout, or I'll just walk to the back of the room. And the thing is, nothing is ever really urgent. I just have a hard time staying in my chair when I'm supposed to.
Have you had this same difficulty sitting still since childhood?

Yes, I have. Actually, even when I was a little girl, my old report cards always said that I was bright, but that I just couldn't stay in my seat or wait my turn. My mother used to joke about it... she'd say I wore a path right into the floor between my desk and the pencil sharpener before I was even ten years old. So, yes, it's been going on for a very long time.
Do you often find yourself arguing with or actively refusing to do what teachers, supervisors, or other authority figures ask?

No, I don't do that at all. I mean, being a teacher myself, I certainly respect the rules and the administration. I don't argue with my principal or refuse to do what's asked of me. Like I said, I might get a bit restless during a long meeting, but I'm not defiant or anything. I just do my job.
Do you often find yourself worrying a lot, even when there isn’t an immediate problem?

No, not really. I mean, I have the usual stress that comes with teaching, but... no, I wouldn't say I worry a lot. If there isn't an actual problem to deal with right in front of me, I don't really sit around stressing over what-ifs. I might be restless, like I said, but it's definitely not because I'm anxious about things.
